option_description: Attests that access decisions are made server-side through a single reusable deny-by-default enforcement layer covering function-level and request-method (POST/PUT/DELETE) authorization, never trusting client-supplied role/flag values.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken access control (IDOR / BOLA / missing function-level authz)" (fires when authz_enforced_server_side_centrally is_false) and of "Privilege escalation via metadata/parameter tampering & mass assignment" (also fires is_false). Client-side-only or scattered per-handler authz fires both exposures (CWE-862/863, T1190/T1548).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Code/design review confirms authorization checks live in a shared component invoked on every protected action, deny-by-default; client-side-only checks or scattered per-handler logic = insecure.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Code/design review confirms authorization checks live in a shared component invoked on every protected action, deny-by-default; client-side-only checks or scattered per-handler logic = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 Broken Access Control

how_to_obtain.instruction: Issue a privileged request with a low-privilege token and confirm a function-level authorization denial.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 403 for a principal lacking the function-level right (secure); 200/204 success = missing function-level authorization (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 — API8 Security Misconfiguration

option_description: Attests that every record access verifies the authenticated principal owns / is entitled to the specific object id (queries scoped by subject), never accepting a user-controlled key as proof of authorization.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken access control (IDOR / BOLA / missing function-level authz)" — fires when object_level_authz_ownership_enforced is_false, yielding IDOR/BOLA (CWE-639, T1190) where one principal reads/modifies another's records by id.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request another user's object id with a different user's token and confirm access is denied.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 403/404 when accessing another tenant's/user's object id (secure ownership check); 200 returning userB's data = IDOR/BOLA (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP API Security Top 10 — Broken Object Property Level Authorization

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect record-fetch code paths for subject-scoped queries.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Data-access queries are scoped by the authenticated subject (e.g. WHERE owner_id = :current_user), not by the raw client-supplied id alone.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 Broken Access Control

option_description: Attests that every non-public route requires an authenticated principal before business logic runs, with default-deny on unmatched/protected routes (global filter / per-route guard) and an explicit small public allowlist.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of both "Broken access control (IDOR / BOLA / missing function-level authz)" and "Broken authentication / session hijacking & weak JWT validation" — fires when authn_enforced_on_every_endpoint is_false, allowing forced-browsing to privileged routes without a session/token (T1190/T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the route/middleware map for global default-deny authentication coverage.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Review route/middleware map: a global authentication filter or per-route guard covers all non-allowlisted endpoints; the public allowlist is explicit and small. Insecure: auth applied per-handler ad hoc with gaps.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 Broken Access Control

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt to reach a privileged route unauthenticated.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 401/403 without a valid session/token (secure); 200 with protected content returned unauthenticated (insecure — forced browsing).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP ASVS V13 — API and Web Service (5.0)

option_description: Attests that repeated access-control / authorization failures (403/authz-denied) are emitted to the log/SIEM and trigger alerting on anomalous volume.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken access control (IDOR / BOLA / missing function-level authz)" — fires when access_control_failures_logged_and_alerted is_false, opening the detectability gap where forced-browsing and IDOR/BOLA scanning go unobserved.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm authz-denied events reach the log/SIEM and that anomalous-volume alerting is configured.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 403/authz-denied events are emitted to the log/SIEM and admins are alerted on anomalous volume. No authz-failure telemetry = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 Broken Access Control

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm logged security events carry timeline metadata and no leaked secrets.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Logs contain authn/authz/validation-failure events with who/what/when; they contain no plaintext passwords, session tokens, full PAN, or PII (CWE-532). Absent security events or leaked secrets = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP ASVS V7 — Error Handling and Logging

option_description: Attests that HTTP request parameters are bound onto domain objects through an explicit bindable-field allow-list / strong-parameters / DTO layer, so privileged fields (isAdmin/role) cannot be over-posted.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Privilege escalation via metadata/parameter tampering & mass assignment" — fires when bindable_field_allowlist_enforced is_false (whole request body bound wholesale to a privilege-bearing entity), enabling mass-assignment privilege escalation (T1068).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm request binding uses an explicit allow-list / strong-parameters / DTO mapping.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Request binding uses explicit field allow-lists / strong parameters / DTOs. Insecure: whole request body bound directly to an entity that has privilege fields.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Mass Assignment Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt to over-post a privileged field and confirm it is ignored/rejected.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Privileged field ignored/rejected (secure); response reflects elevated role = mass-assignment/over-posting (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 Broken Access Control

option_description: Attests that the service cryptographically verifies the JWT signature against a server-pinned expected algorithm and key (not the token-declared header alg) and validates exp/iss/aud.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of both "Broken authentication / session hijacking & weak JWT validation" and "Privilege escalation via metadata/parameter tampering & mass assignment" — fires when jwt_signature_verified is_false, allowing forged/tampered tokens (including role claims) to be trusted (T1550.004/T1068).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the token verifier for pinned-algorithm signature verification and claim checks.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Verifier pins algorithm and validates exp/iss/aud; library is configured to reject alg=none and key-confusion. Insecure: trusts token-declared alg or skips claim checks.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8725 — JSON Web Token Best Current Practices

option_description: Whether the token verifier accepts the unsecured 'alg':'none' JWT (no signature) as valid; true means unsigned tokens are honored.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken authentication / session hijacking & weak JWT validation" — fires when accepts_alg_none is_true, enabling trivial token forgery (T1550.004).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Submit an alg=none token to the verifier and confirm it is rejected.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An alg=none (unsigned) token is rejected (secure, accepts_alg_none=false); if it is accepted as authenticated, accepts_alg_none=true (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8725 — JSON Web Token Best Current Practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the verifier's allowed-algorithm configuration.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Verifier pins algorithm and validates exp/iss/aud; library is configured to reject alg=none and key-confusion. Insecure: trusts token-declared alg or skips claim checks.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8725 — JSON Web Token Best Current Practices

option_description: Whether the verifier trusts the token-declared algorithm and would accept an HS256-signed token verified against the RSA public key (RS256->HS256 key-confusion); true means tokens can be forged using the public key as an HMAC secret.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken authentication / session hijacking & weak JWT validation" — fires when rs256_to_hs256_confusion_possible is_true, enabling token forgery via algorithm confusion (T1550.004).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Submit an HS256 token signed with the RSA public key and confirm it is rejected.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An HS256 token signed with the RSA public key is rejected because the verifier pins the expected algorithm (secure, confusion not possible); acceptance = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8725 — JSON Web Token Best Current Practices

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the verifier pins the expected algorithm rather than trusting the header alg.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Verifier pins algorithm and validates exp/iss/aud; library is configured to reject alg=none and key-confusion. Insecure: trusts token-declared alg or skips claim checks.
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 8725 — JSON Web Token Best Current Practices

option_description: Whether session cookies are issued with the Secure attribute so they are only transmitted over TLS.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken authentication / session hijacking & weak JWT validation" — fires when cookie_secure_flag is_false, allowing the session cookie to leak over cleartext and be hijacked (T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Set-Cookie header for the session cookie's attributes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Set-Cookie carries Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict|Lax (secure). Missing Secure/HttpOnly or SameSite=None-without-Secure = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether session cookies are issued with the HttpOnly attribute so they are inaccessible to client-side script.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken authentication / session hijacking & weak JWT validation" — fires when cookie_httponly_flag is_false, letting XSS exfiltrate the session cookie (T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Set-Cookie header for the session cookie's HttpOnly attribute.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Set-Cookie carries Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict|Lax (secure). Missing Secure/HttpOnly or SameSite=None-without-Secure = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether session cookies set a SameSite attribute (Strict/Lax, and Secure when None) to constrain cross-site transmission.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken authentication / session hijacking & weak JWT validation" — fires when samesite_attribute_set is_false, exposing the cookie to cross-site request contexts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Set-Cookie header for the session cookie's SameSite attribute.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Set-Cookie carries Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict|Lax (secure). Missing Secure/HttpOnly or SameSite=None-without-Secure = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether the session identifier is regenerated on authentication and on privilege change.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken authentication / session hijacking & weak JWT validation" — fires when session_id_regenerated_on_auth is_false, where a pre-authentication session id persists and enables session fixation (T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Compare the session id before and after login and confirm it changes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A fresh session id is issued post-login (Set-Cookie differs from the pre-auth id), and again on privilege elevation (secure); an unchanged id = session fixation (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm session id regeneration on authentication and role change in code/design review.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Session id is regenerated post-authentication and on role change; logout invalidates server-side session / short-lived-or-revoked JWT.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 Broken Access Control

option_description: Whether sessions / JWTs can be invalidated server-side on logout or compromise (server-side session store or short-lived-plus-revocable tokens).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Broken authentication / session hijacking & weak JWT validation" — fires when server_side_revocation_supported is_false, where issued tokens/sessions remain valid until expiry and cannot be killed on logout.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm logout/compromise can invalidate active sessions/tokens server-side.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Session id is regenerated post-authentication and on role change; logout invalidates server-side session / short-lived-or-revoked JWT.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 Broken Access Control

option_description: Attests that all data-store access uses parameterized/prepared statements or safe ORM bindings.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Injection (SQLi / NoSQLi / OS command / LDAP)" — fires when parameterized_queries_used is_false, the primary A03:2021 SQLi/NoSQLi defect (T1190/T1505.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep data-access code for concatenated request data and confirm prepared-statement/bind usage.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Query construction uses placeholders/bind variables throughout; any string-concatenated SQL with request data is an injection finding.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that user-controlled input is concatenated/interpolated into query strings (raw SQL/NoSQL/LDAP filter construction with request data).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Injection (SQLi / NoSQLi / OS command / LDAP)" — fires when dynamic_query_string_concatenation is_true, the direct SQLi/NoSQLi/LDAP-injection sink that parameterization eliminates (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep data-access code for string concatenation/interpolation of request data into queries.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Query construction uses placeholders/bind variables throughout; any string-concatenated SQL with request data is an injection finding (sets this true).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that user data is embedded into an OS shell command string (Runtime.exec(string), subprocess shell=True, child_process.exec).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Injection (SQLi / NoSQLi / OS command / LDAP)" — fires when user_input_in_shell_command_string is_true, the OS-command-injection sink (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep for shell-command execution built from request data.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No shell-string command built from user input; calls use argument arrays (e.g. ProcessBuilder(args[]), subprocess with shell=False). shell=True / exec(string) with user data sets this true.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP OS Command Injection Defense Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that OS command execution is avoided in favour of native libraries, or where unavoidable the argument-array form is used so user data never becomes part of a shell string.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Injection (SQLi / NoSQLi / OS command / LDAP)" — fires when os_commands_avoided_or_arg_array_used is_false (commands built as shell strings), the OS-command-injection defect (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm OS commands are avoided or invoked via argument-array APIs, not a shell string.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No shell-string command built from user input; calls use argument arrays (e.g. ProcessBuilder(args[]), subprocess with shell=False). shell=True / exec(string) with user data = injection risk.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP OS Command Injection Defense Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that untrusted input is validated server-side at the trust boundary with allow-lists (type, length, charset, range).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Injection (SQLi / NoSQLi / OS command / LDAP)" — fires when server_side_allowlist_validation is_false (no server-side allow-list gates input feeding queries/commands).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm each input has a server-side allow-list schema enforced even when the UI also validates.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each input has a server-side schema/allow-list (type, length, charset, range); validation is enforced server-side even when the UI also validates.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that input validation is performed only client-side (UI) and not re-enforced server-side, so an attacker bypassing the UI submits unvalidated input.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Injection (SQLi / NoSQLi / OS command / LDAP)" — fires when validation_is_client_side_only is_true; client-only validation provides no real boundary protection.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm input validation is re-enforced server-side rather than existing only in the UI.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each input has a server-side schema/allow-list (type, length, charset, range); validation is enforced server-side even when the UI also validates. Validation existing only in the UI sets this true.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that input is filtered with deny-lists / blacklist-of-bad-characters rather than allow-lists.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Injection (SQLi / NoSQLi / OS command / LDAP)" — fires when denylist_filtering_used is_true; deny-list filtering is bypassable (encoding, alternate syntax), the insecure A03:2021 input-handling pattern.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review input-filtering logic for reliance on deny-lists / bad-character blacklists rather than allow-lists.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each input has a server-side allow-list (type, length, charset, range); reliance on deny-lists / bad-character blacklists instead sets this true.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that the service validates user-influenced outbound fetch destinations against an allow-list of hosts/schemes/ports (post-DNS-resolution) before issuing the request.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Server-side request forgery (SSRF)" — fires when outbound_fetch_destination_allowlisted is_false (user-supplied URL passed straight to the HTTP client), allowing SSRF to internal services (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the outbound-fetch code path for allow-list enforcement on the resolved destination.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Outbound-fetch code resolves and validates the destination against an allow-list and blocks RFC1918/loopback/link-local + 169.254.169.254 after DNS resolution. Insecure: passes user URL straight to the HTTP client.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Server Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that the service rejects outbound fetches resolving to RFC1918 private ranges, loopback (127.0.0.0/8), and link-local (169.254.0.0/16) after DNS resolution.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Server-side request forgery (SSRF)" — fires when private_and_metadata_targets_blocked is_false, permitting SSRF pivots into the internal network and link-local services (T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the outbound-fetch path rejects private/loopback/link-local destinations after DNS resolution.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Outbound-fetch code resolves and validates the destination against an allow-list and blocks RFC1918/loopback/link-local + 169.254.169.254 after DNS resolution. Insecure: passes user URL straight to the HTTP client.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Server Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that outbound fetches to the cloud instance metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254, and equivalents such as fd00:ec2::254) are explicitly blocked.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Server-side request forgery (SSRF)" — fires when cloud_metadata_endpoint_blocked is_false, allowing workload IAM credential theft via the metadata API (T1552.005).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm outbound fetches to the cloud instance metadata endpoint are explicitly blocked in the egress controls.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Outbound-fetch code resolves and validates the destination against an allow-list and blocks RFC1918/loopback/link-local + 169.254.169.254 after DNS resolution. Insecure: passes user URL straight to the HTTP client.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Server Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that the service natively deserializes attacker-controlled bytes (Java ObjectInputStream.readObject, Python pickle.load, PyYAML yaml.load without SafeLoader, Ruby Marshal.load, PHP unserialize) on untrusted input.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Insecure deserialization & RCE" — fires when native_deserialization_of_untrusted_data is_true, triggering gadget chains leading to RCE (T1190/T1059).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep for native deserialization sinks and confirm none operate on attacker-controlled bytes.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No native deserialization of attacker-controlled bytes (Java readObject, Python pickle.load, yaml.load without SafeLoader, PHP unserialize). Insecure if any operate on untrusted input (sets this true).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Deserialization Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests that where serialized objects are unavoidable, payloads are integrity-protected (HMAC/signature verified before deserializing) AND deserialization is type-constrained to a strict class allow-list (look-ahead/resolveClass filter, ObjectInputFilter, SafeConstructor).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Insecure deserialization & RCE" — fires when deserialization_class_allowlist_or_signed_payloads is_false (deserialization unauthenticated and unconstrained) (T1190/T1059).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a class allow-list / object-input filter and an HMAC-or-signature check guard every deserialization entry point.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No native deserialization of attacker-controlled bytes; where serialization is required, payloads are integrity-protected (HMAC) and type-constrained (class allow-list / ObjectInputFilter / SafeConstructor) before deserializing. Unauthenticated/unconstrained deserialization sets this false.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Deserialization Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether untrusted data is contextually output-encoded via framework auto-escaping (HTML/attribute/JS/URL context) before rendering.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Cross-site scripting (XSS) / missing output encoding" — fires when contextual_output_encoding_applied is_false, where reflected/stored/DOM XSS executes attacker script in victim browsers (T1059.007/T1539).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm output goes through framework auto-escaping and grep for raw-HTML escape-hatches.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output goes through framework auto-escaping; raw-HTML escape-hatches are absent or justified+sanitized. Each hit is an XSS sink to review.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Cross-Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether raw-HTML escape-hatches that bypass auto-escaping are present and fed untrusted data (e.g. dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML=, v-html, bypassSecurityTrust, Jinja |safe, render_template_string).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Cross-site scripting (XSS) / missing output encoding" — fires when unsafe_html_sinks_used is_true, an XSS injection sink (T1059.007).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep for raw-HTML sinks fed untrusted data.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output goes through framework auto-escaping; raw-HTML escape-hatches are absent or justified+sanitized. Each hit is an XSS sink to review (sets this true).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Cross-Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether the service emits an enforcing Content-Security-Policy response header (e.g. default-src 'self') as defense-in-depth against script injection.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Cross-site scripting (XSS) / missing output encoding" — fires when content_security_policy_enforced is_false, removing the CSP backstop limiting injected-script execution (T1059.007).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect response headers for an enforcing Content-Security-Policy (not report-only).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All five present with hardened values (HSTS max-age>=63072000; CSP default-src 'self'; nosniff; DENY/frame-ancestors). Missing headers = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secure Headers Project

option_description: Whether the deployed CSP weakens script protection by permitting 'unsafe-inline' and/or 'unsafe-eval' script sources.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Cross-site scripting (XSS) / missing output encoding" — fires when csp_allows_unsafe_inline_or_eval is_true, nullifying CSP's XSS mitigation (T1059.007).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the CSP script-src directives for 'unsafe-inline' and/or 'unsafe-eval'.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CSP uses default-src/script-src 'self' (with nonces/hashes) and no 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval' (secure); presence of 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' in script-src sets this true.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secure Headers Project

option_description: Whether credentials/keys are baked into source/config files or IaC templates (Terraform/Helm/Compose) rather than pulled from a secret manager and injected at runtime.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Hardcoded / leaked secrets & over-privileged service identity" — fires when secrets_hardcoded_in_config_or_iac is_true; hardcoded secrets are harvested from the repo/artifact and reused against downstream stores (T1552.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan source/config/IaC for literal credential values.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No literal secret values in repo; references resolve to a secret manager (Vault/AWS Secrets Manager/etc.) at runtime. Any literal credential sets this true.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet

option_description: Whether the workload identity and downstream credentials are least-privilege and scoped per workload (scoped_per_workload) versus a shared superuser/root/standing-admin credential reused across services (shared_admin_or_root).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Hardcoded / leaked secrets & over-privileged service identity" — fires when least_privilege_service_identity eq "shared_admin_or_root", turning any foothold into broad downstream compromise (T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the workload's downstream credentials for per-workload least-privilege scoping.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Workload identity (e.g. per-service ServiceAccount/SPIFFE/IAM role) maps to narrowly-scoped downstream grants; DB role lacks SUPERUSER/CREATEROLE. Insecure: one broad credential reused across services.
how_to_obtain.source: HashiCorp Vault — Database secrets engine

option_description: Whether calls to data stores and downstream services use TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation (tls_validated) versus cleartext or insecure_skip_verify / rejectUnauthorized:false / sslmode=disable (plaintext_or_skip_verify).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Hardcoded / leaked secrets & over-privileged service identity" — fires when downstream_tls_enforced_and_validated eq "plaintext_or_skip_verify", letting harvested or in-flight credentials be intercepted (T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect downstream client configuration for certificate-validation bypass flags.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No certificate-validation bypass flags; downstream clients configured TLS 1.2+ with validation on. Any skip-verify/disable hit = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP ASVS V9 — Communications

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the TLS versions/ciphers the downstream endpoint accepts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLS 1.2/1.3 with strong (AEAD/ECDHE) cipher suites accepted on the downstream endpoint the service connects to.
how_to_obtain.source: Nmap ssl-enum-ciphers NSE script

option_description: Attests that production returns generic error responses with debug mode off — stack traces, framework debug pages, and detailed internal messages are not exposed to clients.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Security misconfiguration — verbose errors, debug, defaults & unpatched components" — fires when debug_and_verbose_errors_disabled_in_prod is_false, leaking internals that aid further attack (A05:2021, T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request a route with malformed input and confirm a generic error body with no stack trace/debug page.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Generic error body + correct status, no stack trace/framework debug page/internal path or query text. Leaked stack trace or debug console = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration

option_description: Attests that all default/sample accounts and default passwords shipped with the platform, framework, or appliance have been removed or had their credentials changed.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Security misconfiguration — verbose errors, debug, defaults & unpatched components" — fires when default_accounts_removed_or_changed is_false, leaving a trivial compromise path (A05:2021, T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Audit the account and credential baseline for remaining default/sample accounts or default passwords.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Default credentials removed/changed; sample apps, admin consoles, and unused features disabled; config baseline reviewed and version-controlled (CM-2/CM-6). Defaults left in place = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Top 10 A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration

option_description: Attests that unnecessary features, sample applications, admin consoles, debug endpoints, unused ports, and superfluous services are disabled or removed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Audit enabled features and exposed endpoints/ports; confirm sample apps, debug endpoints, and admin consoles not needed in production are disabled.

option_description: Attests that the service configuration follows a documented, reviewed, version-controlled secure baseline (NIST CM-2/CM-6), so hardening is repeatable and drift is detectable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a reviewed, version-controlled secure-baseline document exists and is current, with CM linkage.

option_description: Attests that Software Composition Analysis (SCA) runs continuously in CI against all direct and nested dependencies, producing a current component inventory checked against CVE/NVD.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Security misconfiguration — verbose errors, debug, defaults & unpatched components" — fires when dependency_vulnerability_scanning_enabled is_false, where dependency versions are un-inventoried (A06:2021, T1195.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify an SCA step runs in the build pipeline against all dependencies and that its component inventory is current.

option_description: Whether one or more direct or nested dependencies (OS packages, runtimes, libraries, app/web server, DBMS, APIs) are known-vulnerable, unsupported, or out-of-date with unremediated CVEs, or are unmaintained.

option_description: Attests that deployed artifacts/images are obtained from official sources over secure (TLS) links and their signatures/provenance (SLSA in-toto / cosign / signed packages) are verified against a pinned identity before deployment.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers of "Security misconfiguration — verbose errors, debug, defaults & unpatched components" — fires when artifact_supply_chain_signed_provenance_verified is_false (artifacts pulled unsigned/unverified), permitting malicious substitution (A06:2021, SLSA v1.0, T1195.001).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the deploy pipeline verifies artifact signatures/provenance against a pinned identity before deployment.
